title: Prevent delayed prior fragments from contaminating replacement SCHC sessions
description: Security review of spec/03-adaptation.md §5.6 and draft-lichen-schc-lora-00 terminal hold-down found that the 60-second tombstone does not fully disambiguate packets when T=0. During hold-down, regular late fragments are discarded without a normative tombstone high-water update; after expiry, any Regular/All-1 with counter greater than the stored high-water may create a session. Once a replacement session is active, there is also no rule requiring every admitted fragment to be newer than an immutable session-admission floor. Because the link replay window accepts unseen out-of-order counters, a delayed authenticated fragment from the prior packet can create or contaminate a replacement context, especially when duplicate retransmissions were allocated after the frame that produced terminal success. Define a safe session-opening/admission barrier (or a bounded lifetime/DTag mechanism) that cannot admit prior-packet fragments, advance the relevant terminal barrier on every authenticated late message, and add state-machine vectors for delayed unique regular/All-1 frames both during hold-down and after a replacement starts.
notes: Rust complete: only regular W=0 FCN=62 opens T=0; every authenticated late message advances terminal high-water; expired tombstone remains durable admission floor; replacement session enforces immutable counter floor. Restart floor persistence is signed, anti-rollback, trust/replay committed, exact-generation gated. Full tests/lints pass.
